hypotheses:
Work is done only when you have been shown it working the way you chose: for every requirement the AI works out the best proof to show you and recommends it, and you decide what the proof is. Done and the merge are refused until that proof's evidence is recorded. Checking is by the tests that cover what changed, not the whole suite, and a merge is never green while an affected acceptance test lacks a passing run.
will: Give every requirement a proof of how you will see it working, recommended by the AI after researching what fits the change, decided by you through the question tool or your own words.
will: Plan the code a proof needs, record the proof's evidence and where to see it once shown, and refuse done and the merge for a touched requirement without it (a proof that can only be shown after the landing does not hold the merge; it is asked for the turn after).
will: Hold the merge while an acceptance test the change can affect fails or has no passing run on the current tree and environment, a regression is unresolved, or a named full run is pending.
will: Select each turn's tests by the functions they executed and the requirement's linked tests, from a grep-able test map, reusing evidence only on an exact match.
will: Run the full suite only for a named reason (shared test infrastructure), at most once per merge check, and let you waive it for one exact change through the question tool.
will: Route a proof or a test that cannot settle (a broken environment, a missing tool) to the debug workflow.
won't: Count a passing test suite as the proof of a change you see.
won't: Let a missing proof pass the merge with only a mention (the earlier rule).
won't: Ask you for a record id or a shell command, or to read a proof the AI wrote in order to approve it.
won't: Ask you about a regression or a failing test; they hold the merge until fixed.
won't: Run the full suite routinely, or in place of an empty selection.
won't: Let the agent waive a full run or a proof on your behalf.

Then I'd like to understand in the previous session what went wrong with iaso that led to the fact that we still have this issue. And of course I need you to apply the proposed fixes. You can add the relevant steps to the ongoing workflow.

Question: When you asked me to apply the proposed fixes, did you mean that a merge should be held by failing or unrun acceptance tests, with only the tests that cover the change being run?

Earlier today you confirmed a close wording: "Yes, hold the merge on failing acceptance tests".
Options: Yes, hold merges on failing or unrun tests, running only the tests the change covers (Recommended) (Merges are held when an acceptance test of a touched requirement fails or has no passing run, and each turn runs only the tests that cover what changed. Recommended: Your words ask to catch issues earlier and to apply the proposed fixes, so a test hold that is limited to the tests a change covers matches that.); No, apply only the proof gate and leave the test hold and test selection out (Done and the merge are refused only for a missing shown proof; failing or unrun tests do not hold a merge.); Some of them, and I will name which (Only the fixes I name are applied; the rest are left out until I decide them.)
Answer: Yes, hold merges on failing or unrun tests, running only the tests the change covers (Recommended)

You said on 2026-11-04: "Then, I wish to capture those issues earlier. Instead of saying: this is merged, it should work, we need claude code and iaso to actually show the user it is working.
